messages:
samir: Heads-up — I'm going to roll a canary in staging to replace the single NAT GW with the new shared egress pool (ha-nat-pool). Wanted to surface the TF plan and get quick eyes on route priority / PrivateLink reachability before I apply.

priya: SGTM. can you paste the terraform diff? big things to watch: route table assoc ordering, any hard-coded EIP refs, and k8s egress annotations.

samir: pasted plan excerpt below (trimmed):
```
# module.egress.aws_eip.pool[0] will be created
+ resource "aws_eip" "pool" {count = 2} 
# module.egress.aws_nat_gateway.main[0] will be created
+ resource "aws_nat_gateway" "main" {count = 2, allocation_id = aws_eip.pool[0].id} 
# aws_route.private_to_egress will be changed in-place
~ resource "aws_route" "private_to_egress" {priority = 100 -> 90}
# aws_route_table_association.app_subnet_assoc will be replaced
- resource "aws_route_table_association" "app_subnet_assoc" {..} -> + resource "aws_route_table_association" "app_subnet_assoc" {..}
```

samir: Also adding a small module to tag EIPs with "redwood:egress=ha-pool" so the new pool can be discovered by some on-prem infra scripts.

alex: Quick Q: PrivateLink endpoints for S3 and SecretsManager are in the same subnets — are we changing the route table for those subnets? If we assoc a different RT before the PL endpoints are created it could break access.

samir: Good catch. Plan changes RT assoc for app-subnets only; private service subnets (vpce-*) are not in the same list. But one subtlety: the route table change has replace semantics right now, which will briefly detach the association. I can switch to a create-new-assoc + delete-old step instead to avoid downtime.

danielle: For the k8s nodes, remember we have node-level egress via NAT and pod egress via ENI for some clusters. The TF change should not change node_egress_security_group tags. If you mutate the subnet's map_public_ip_on_launch or change the route to IGW it could flip behaviour.

samir: Not touching map_public_ip_on_launch. Only route entries. Also updated the module to do an ordered apply: 1) create EIPs and nat -> 2) create new route tables and new associations -> 3) flip routes -> 4) remove old associations. Will rely on lifecycle create_before_destroy on assoc.

priya: Can you show the terraform snippet for the assoc lifecycle?

samir: sure:
```hcl
resource "aws_route_table_association" "app_subnet_assoc" {
  subnet_id = var.subnet_id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.app_rt.id

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
    prevent_destroy = false
  }
}
```

infra-bot: plan summary: 
+ 3 to add, ~1 to change, -2 to destroy (will show full plan shortly)

alex: LGTM but two asks: 1) add a plan output filter with the explicit list of affected subnet ids so SRE duty can watch them, 2) ensure the replace of assoc is not simultaneous across AZs — stagger by AZ to avoid cross-AZ dependency blast radius.

samir: will do both. I'll add a `for_each` with az shard keys and a small `sleep` in the apply wrapper to stagger. Also will post the exact subnet list and a quick rollback step (re-assoc old RTs and drain nat eips) before I apply.

danielle: FYI — if you run into an EIP quota, talk to infra-ops early. Staging quota ok today but prod is tight.

priya: +1 to staged rollout. once you have the final plan and subnet list drop it here and we can give a single thumbs-up to proceed. :thumbsup:

samir: thanks — posting final plan + affected_subnets in ~20m. tagging @alex @priya @danielle for visibility.
